name: ES Closing Auction Value Ratchet v1
instrument: ES continuous front-month signal with one MES execution unit
hypothesis: The opening auction establishes the cash session's initial accepted-value center. If the cumulative cash-session center has migrated away from it by 13:59 and price is already beyond the migrated center in the same direction, closing-session participants inherit directional inventory rather than a balanced book. That inventory should have positive convexity into the closing liquidity window.

rules.opening_center: volume-weighted mean of one-minute typical price during the opening auction
rules.cumulative_center: volume-weighted mean of one-minute typical price during the cumulative auction
rules.long_signal: cumulative center > opening center and 13:59 close > cumulative center
rules.short_signal: cumulative center < opening center and 13:59 close < cumulative center
rules.entry: 14:00 open plus one adverse ES tick
rules.stop_fill: cumulative auction center plus one adverse ES tick
rules.entry_validity: skip if the frozen stop fill is not adverse to the simulated entry
rules.same_bar_rule: if the 14:00 entry bar touches the stop trigger, assume the stop fills
rules.gap_through_rule: if a stop bar opens beyond the trigger, fill at the worse bar open plus one adverse tick; otherwise fill at the frozen stop price
rules.survivor_exit: 15:55 open plus one adverse ES tick
rules.position_limit: one MES and at most one trade per RTH session

lesson: Late-session price leading a migrated cumulative center was a 2022-dominated effect rather than a stable closing-handoff edge. The closing clock alone does not turn value migration into robust persistence. No year, side, distance, or volatility filter is permitted.
holdout_policy: 2024-2025 was not evaluated because the unchanged rule failed its development stability gate.
prohibited_posthoc_changes: volume, volatility, weekday, or regime filters
